purpose: Teach: 水中/乾い/細く/硬い/吸い/触る/弾け/滑っ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、水中で泳ぐの、大好きだった。
lines.en: When I was young, I loved swimming underwater.
lines.style: Soft opening, as if surfacing from memory. Quiet, steady pace. Gentle warmth—not wistful yet, just present in the recollection. Lets the sentence breathe at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。庭の洗濯物、太陽で、よく乾いたわね。
lines.en: Yes. The laundry in the garden dried so well in the sun.
lines.style: Warm and present. A small nod of agreement that becomes its own memory. Light, unhurried. The voice of someone tending to both conversation and remembrance at once.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お前の手、年月で、細くなったな。
lines.en: Your hands have gotten thinner over the years.
lines.style: Observant, intimate. Not sad—noting a fact with tenderness. Voice rests on the word 'hands' like a gentle touch. Slow, careful delivery. Acceptance beneath the surface.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 最近、お餅、硬いの、苦手になったわ。
lines.en: I've had trouble with hard mochi lately.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact but without complaint. A small sigh beneath the words—age as simple fact. Conversational, accepting. The voice of someone stating something true about themselves without drama.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: コーヒー、ストローで吸い続けたら、変な顔されたな。
lines.en: I kept sucking on my coffee through a straw and got some odd looks.
lines.style: A small, dry laugh in the telling. Lightweight delivery—finding humor in the small embarrassment. Wry but not bitter. The voice of someone who's learned to laugh at his own strangeness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お互いの手、触ると、いつも安心するね。
lines.en: When we hold each other's hands, I always feel at ease.
lines.style: Tender and unhurried. Each word placed with care, like hands finding their place in the dark. Quiet conviction. The voice that says something true that doesn't need to be said often.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 花火、最後の一発、見事に弾けた。
lines.en: That last firework burst so beautifully.
lines.style: Wistful but grounded. The opening carries the image upward. Slight rise in wonder on 'burst.' A moment held—not mourning the past, but honoring it. Trailing softly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 濡れた廊下、滑って転んじゃダメよ。
lines.en: Don't slip and fall on the wet hallway.
lines.style: Practical care wrapped in gentleness. A soft caution, not an alarm. The voice of someone who has learned to say 'I need you to be careful' through the small things. Warm but watchful.
